title: Pricing Resistance
trigger_description: The prospect reacts to the price before the value is clear to them.
fact: Gong (11,331 opportunities): deals where price was discussed on call 1 won 42% of the time vs 5% when price was never discussed; star reps raise it in the last quarter of the call after value is built.
impact: Price pushback usually means the return isn't obvious yet, not that the budget is missing. Defending the number locks the conversation on cost.
act: I hear you, and honestly when something feels expensive it usually means the return is not clear yet, and that is on me to fix. Before we talk about the number, let me put it next to what the current way of working is costing you every month.
act_hinglish: Samajh sakta hoon, aur sach kahun toh jab koi cheez expensive lagti hai, uska matlab hota hai return abhi clear nahi hai, aur woh meri zimmedari hai. Number pe aane se pehle, ek baar dekh lete hain ki abhi ka tareeka aapko har mahine kitna cost kar raha hai.
question_to_ask: When you say expensive, is that compared to the budget you had in mind, or compared to another option you are weighing?
proof_point: Quantify the pain in INR per month from what the prospect already told you; only quote numbers from the capsule.
do_not: Do not defend the price or offer a discount immediately.
psychology: Price pushback signals certainty failure, not budget absence. Shift the burden of thought from cost to ROI clarity.

title: Skepticism Defense
trigger_description: The prospect doubts the claim because a previous tool or vendor disappointed them.
fact: Indian buyers are described as cautious software buyers 'due to past negative experiences, not price objections'; references and clear pilot results are the remedies named.
impact: Skeptics fear being wrong again. Generic feature lists confirm the fear; specific, curious inquiry collapses it.
act: That is a fair reaction, and if every tool delivered what it promised, nobody would be skeptical. I would rather not repeat whatever went wrong last time, so walk me through what was promised and what actually happened, and I will tell you straight whether we would be any different.
act_hinglish: Yeh bilkul fair reaction hai, agar har tool apna promise poora karta toh koi skeptical hota hi nahi. Main nahi chahta ki pichli baar jo galat hua woh dobara ho, toh mujhe batayiye kya promise kiya gaya tha aur actually kya hua, aur main seedha bata dunga ki hum alag honge ya nahi.
question_to_ask: What exactly did the last tool promise that did not happen, and how did your team find out?
proof_point: One named reference in the same city or industry plus a defined pilot with a success metric and a decision date.
do_not: Avoid reciting generic feature lists or saying 'we're different'.
psychology: Skeptics fear being wrong again due to past overpromised tools. Specificity and curious inquiry collapse defensive barriers.

title: Delay & "Think About It"
trigger_description: A passive delay without a stated reason or date.
fact: JOLT (2.5M calls): 40–60% of lost deals end in no decision; 87% of deals show moderate or high buyer indecision. Gong: no next step discussed means a 5% close rate vs 20% with one.
impact: Delay is never about time; it is an unspoken objection. Accepting it without a date is how deals ghost.
act: Of course, take the time you need. In my experience though, when someone wants to think it over there is usually one specific thing that does not feel fully justified yet, and I would rather address that now than leave you to work it out alone from an email.
act_hinglish: Bilkul, aap time lijiye. Lekin mere experience mein jab koi sochna chahta hai, toh usually ek specific cheez hoti hai jo abhi poori tarah justify nahi lagti, aur main chahunga ki woh abhi discuss kar lein, email ke bharose chhodne se accha hai.
question_to_ask: If we set the timing aside for a moment, is there anything about the fit itself that still feels uncertain to you?
proof_point: Offer a recommendation and a dated next step with the right person on the invite rather than more information.
do_not: Never accept a passive delay without discovering the root objection and setting a date.
psychology: Delay is never about time; it is about an unspoken internal objection. Surface the hidden blocker before ghosting occurs.

title: Ego & Autonomy Buyer
trigger_keywords: we have done this for years
trigger_description: A senior buyer who defends their current setup and their authority.
fact: Challenger's Commercial Teaching works when the reframe targets the business problem, not the person; practitioners warn against forcing all six steps into one meeting.
impact: Challenging the person threatens executive identity and ends the conversation. Challenging the operational gap with logical tension keeps it open.
act: You clearly know this business far better than I ever will, so I am not here to teach you anything about it. What I am curious about is this: if the current setup were fully solving the problem, you probably would not have taken this meeting, so something made you say yes.
act_hinglish: Aap apna business mujhse kahin better jaante hain, toh main aapko kuch sikhane nahi aaya. Mujhe bas yeh jaanna hai: agar abhi ka setup problem poori tarah solve kar raha hota, toh aap yeh meeting shayad lete hi nahi, toh kisi cheez ne aapko haan bolne pe majboor kiya.
question_to_ask: What would have to break at twice today's volume for this problem to become urgent for you?
proof_point: A peer story (same industry, similar scale) about what changed, told in two sentences, not a feature list.
do_not: Do not out-expert or debate the buyer directly.
psychology: Challenging ego threatens executive identity. Challenge the operational gap with logical tension, never the person.

title: Competitive Pressure
trigger_description: The prospect names or hints at another vendor they are comparing you with.
fact: Gong: discussing competitors early in the cycle raises win likelihood; discussing them late lowers it. In closing calls the only discriminator is which topics the buyer raises.
impact: Feature comparisons commoditize you. Framing the decision around the number that matters and the risk of each option keeps you out of the checklist.
act: It is good that you are comparing, you should. I would just suggest the question is not which tool has more features, because on a checklist we will all look similar. The real question is which one actually changes the number that matters for your business, and that is what I would like to compare.
act_hinglish: Accha hai ki aap compare kar rahe hain, karna bhi chahiye. Main bas yeh kahunga ki sawaal yeh nahi hai ki kis tool mein zyada features hain, kyunki checklist pe hum sab same dikhenge. Asli sawaal yeh hai ki kaun sa tool aapke business ka woh number badalta hai jo matter karta hai, aur wahi compare karna chahiye.
question_to_ask: What have you seen from them so far that you liked, and what is still missing for you?
proof_point: Name one capability the capsule lists that maps to their stated decision criterion; never improvise a comparison.
do_not: Never trash-talk competitors or trigger a feature-by-feature checklist.
psychology: Feature comparisons commoditize you. Frame the decision around actual bottom-line velocity and risk elimination.

title: "It's too expensive"
trigger_description: A direct price objection, often a smokescreen for unclear value.
fact: Gong's objection data (67,149 demos): top performers pause ~5x longer after an objection; average reps launch a ~21-second monologue.
impact: Answering fast with a justification tells the buyer the price is negotiable. A pause and one question tells them you are confident.
act: Okay. Help me understand that a little better before I respond, because I do not want to answer the wrong thing. Is it expensive against the budget you had in mind, or expensive compared with what the problem is already costing you every month?
act_hinglish: Theek hai. Jawab dene se pehle thoda samajhna chahunga, kyunki main galat cheez ka jawab nahi dena chahta. Kya yeh aapke mann mein jo budget tha uske hisaab se expensive hai, ya is problem ki wajah se jo har mahine nuksaan ho raha hai uske hisaab se?
question_to_ask: If the price were not an issue at all, would you want to move forward with this this month?
proof_point: Restate the cost of inaction in INR from their own numbers before touching the price.
do_not: Do not quote a lower number or a discount in your first sentence.
psychology: The isolation question separates a genuine price objection from a smokescreen hiding a different concern.

title: "No budget this quarter"
trigger_description: Budget is said to be unavailable until a later period.
fact: Gong: deals where budget was discussed on call 1 won 49% vs 7% when never discussed. India's financial year ends 31 March; budgets reset in April.
impact: Budget objections are often a timing or sourcing question (opex vs capex, whose line item) rather than a no.
act: Understood, and I would not expect a new line item to appear mid-quarter. Sometimes this kind of spend comes out of this year's operating budget rather than a fresh approval, and sometimes it makes sense to lock the price now and start in the new financial year.
act_hinglish: Samajh gaya, aur quarter ke beech mein naya budget line milna mushkil hota hai. Kabhi kabhi yeh kharcha is saal ke operating budget se ho jaata hai, naye approval ke bina, aur kabhi price abhi lock karke naye financial year mein start karna sahi hota hai.
question_to_ask: Is there an existing budget line this could sit under today, or would it genuinely need a new approval?
proof_point: Offer a phased start (pilot now, full rollout in the new FY) with the price fixed in writing.
do_not: Do not simply agree to call back next quarter without a dated step and a named owner.
psychology: 'No budget' is frequently 'no priority yet'. Linking the spend to a cash outcome moves it up the list.

title: "Next quarter / after Diwali"
trigger_description: The prospect pushes the decision to a later date tied to a calendar event.
fact: Gong classes most timing objections as smokescreens or complacency: isolate first, then return to the current pain rather than handling the date.
impact: Festive season and FY-end are real cycles in India, but they are also the most common cover for indecision.
act: That makes complete sense, the season is busy and nobody wants a new system landing in the middle of it. Let me ask it the other way round though: if timing were not a factor at all, would this be something you would want to go ahead with?
act_hinglish: Yeh bilkul samajh aata hai, season busy hota hai aur koi nahi chahta ki beech mein naya system aaye. Lekin ek baar ulta sochte hain: agar timing bilkul factor na hoti, toh kya aap isko aage badhana chahte?
question_to_ask: Between now and then, does the problem get cheaper to fix or more expensive?
proof_point: Anchor to a natural deadline (31 March, festive stock-up, new FY pricing) with a mutual action plan.
do_not: Do not accept the date as the plan; a date without an owner and a step is a stall.
psychology: Separating 'when' from 'whether' exposes whether the objection is about the calendar or about the fit.

title: "I need to check with my boss / sir"
trigger_description: The person on the call is not the economic buyer.
fact: MEDDPICC: the Economic Buyer has final budget authority and can approve even if others object; a Champion sells for you internally. In Indian SMEs founder approval is common regardless of ticket size.
impact: Letting your contact pitch alone turns them into a weak relay; equipping them or joining them keeps the deal in your hands.
act: Of course, that is how it should work. Rather than leaving you to carry the whole explanation alone, I am happy to do a short twenty-minute walkthrough together with them, so they can ask me the hard questions directly and you do not have to defend something you only saw once.
act_hinglish: Bilkul, aisa hi hona chahiye. Aap akele poora explanation carry karein, uski bajaye main unke saath ek chhota bees minute ka walkthrough kar sakta hoon, taaki mushkil sawaal woh mujhse directly poochein aur aapko ek baar dekhi hui cheez defend na karni pade.
question_to_ask: When your MD looks at a spend like this, what is the first thing they usually check: the cash impact, the risk, or who else is using it?
proof_point: A one-page business case in the buyer's words (pain, cost, outcome) that the champion can forward.
do_not: Do not push the contact to 'convince' their boss; do not treat them as the decision-maker when they said they aren't.
psychology: Authority objections are conditions, not resistance. Map the real buyer and make the champion look good.

title: Buying group / too many stakeholders
trigger_description: Several people must agree and the cycle is slowing down.
fact: Gong: closed-won deals include 67% more contacts than closed-lost. Forrester notes Indian deals involve much larger buyer groups and suffer 'purchase paralysis'.
impact: A single-threaded deal with a buying group is the highest-risk shape there is.
act: That is normal for a decision like this, and I would rather make it easy for the whole group than keep sending you back and forth. If you tell me the three people whose yes matters most, I will prepare exactly what each of them needs to see and we can agree who does what by when.
act_hinglish: Aise decision mein yeh normal hai, aur main chahta hoon poore group ke liye yeh easy ho, aapko baar baar aage peeche bhejne se accha. Agar aap mujhe woh teen log bata dein jinki haan sabse zyada matter karti hai, toh main har ek ke liye exactly wahi prepare karunga jo unhe dekhna hai, aur hum tay kar lenge kaun kya kab karega.
question_to_ask: Who in the group has said no to a purchase like this before, and what was their reason?
proof_point: Propose a mutual action plan with named stakeholders and dates rather than another demo.
do_not: Do not keep selling to one contact and hoping they carry the group.
psychology: Buying groups stall from choice and information overload (JOLT). Narrow the options and name the owners.

title: "We're doing fine as we are"
trigger_description: The prospect sees no pain; this is complacency, not an objection.
fact: Gong's typology: complacency should not be 'handled' as an objection; pause and go back to discovery, build urgency from current pain.
impact: Arguing against 'fine' makes you the problem. Surfacing the hidden cost of the status quo makes the status quo the problem.
act: Good, then honestly there is no reason to change anything unless the current way is quietly costing you something you cannot see from the inside. Can I ask you two quick questions just to check that, and if everything really is fine I will tell you so and we can leave it there.
act_hinglish: Accha hai, toh sach mein kuch badalne ki zaroorat nahi, jab tak abhi ka tareeka chupke se aapko kuch cost na kar raha ho jo andar se dikhta nahi. Kya main bas do chhote sawaal pooch sakta hoon check karne ke liye, aur agar sab sach mein theek hai toh main khud bol dunga aur baat yahin chhod dete hain.
question_to_ask: If your volume doubled next year, what would break first: the people, the process, or the follow-up?
proof_point: A cost-of-inaction estimate in INR per month built from their own numbers (hours, missed follow-ups, delayed receivables).
do_not: Do not pitch features or argue; do not treat 'fine' as a no.
psychology: Status quo bias is strongest when the future state has never been articulated. Make the gap visible before you sell.

title: "We manage in Excel / Tally"
trigger_description: The real competitor is a manual process or an accounting tool.
fact: For many Indian SMBs, SaaS competes with Excel rather than another SaaS; Tally is 'ridiculously sticky'. Buyers often want to not need Tally for a task rather than integrate it.
impact: Excel works until it silently fails: missed follow-ups, no visibility, one person holding the file. The product must save real time or prevent missed revenue.
act: Excel is honestly the toughest competitor we have, because it is free and everyone already knows it, and Tally should absolutely stay for your accounts. The place it usually breaks is the follow-ups nobody remembers and the one person who holds the whole sheet, so I am curious where it breaks for you.
act_hinglish: Excel sach mein hamara sabse tough competitor hai, kyunki woh free hai aur sabko aata hai, aur Tally toh accounts ke liye bilkul rehna chahiye. Jahan yeh usually tootta hai woh hai follow-ups jo kisi ko yaad nahi rehte, aur woh ek insaan jiske paas poori sheet hoti hai, toh mujhe jaanna hai aapke yahan kahan tootta hai.
question_to_ask: How many hours a week go into updating and chasing that sheet, and who owns it when that person is on leave?
proof_point: Show the one workflow that replaces the sheet end to end; keep Tally for accounting and say so.
do_not: Do not mock the spreadsheet or promise to replace Tally for accounting.
psychology: Respecting the current tool lowers defensiveness; the gap, not the tool, is the argument.

title: "Never heard of you"
trigger_description: Vendor-risk concern about a young or unknown company.
fact: HubSpot's taxonomy treats 'never heard of you' as an information request, not a rejection; answer briefly and move to their problem.
impact: Over-explaining the company makes it about you. A short answer plus a question makes it about them.
act: That is fair, we are newer than the big names and I would rather you check us properly than take my word for it. I can connect you with a customer in your industry who you can call directly, and whatever we agree, we would start small enough that trying us is not a risk.
act_hinglish: Yeh fair hai, hum bade naamon se naye hain aur main chahunga aap humein theek se check karein, sirf mera word na lein. Main aapko aapki industry ke ek customer se connect kar sakta hoon jisko aap directly call kar sakein, aur jo bhi tay ho, hum itna chhota start karenge ki humein try karna koi risk na ho.
question_to_ask: What would you need to see from any new vendor to feel safe: references, a pilot, or the people behind it?
proof_point: A same-industry reference and a short pilot with an exit clause.
do_not: Do not launch into the company history or funding story.
psychology: Trust deficits are resolved by specificity and risk reversal, not by assertions of credibility.

title: "X is cheaper"
trigger_description: A competitor's lower price is used as leverage.
fact: Gong: risk-reversal language (opt-outs, SLAs, guarantees) correlated with a 32% win-rate lift; talk-ratio was a bigger lever than discounting.
impact: Matching price concedes the frame. Clarifying what the cheaper quote includes often reveals it is not the same scope.
act: They may well be cheaper, and sometimes the cheaper option genuinely is the right call. What I would want to make sure of is that you are comparing the same thing, because quotes often differ on onboarding, support and the integration you mentioned, and those are where the real cost shows up later.
act_hinglish: Ho sakta hai woh saste hon, aur kabhi kabhi sasta option sach mein sahi hota hai. Main bas yeh pakka karna chahunga ki aap same cheez compare kar rahe hain, kyunki quotes aksar onboarding, support aur jo integration aapne bataya uspe alag hote hain, aur asli cost baad mein wahin dikhti hai.
question_to_ask: What did their quote include for onboarding, support and the integration you mentioned earlier?
proof_point: A side-by-side scope list from the capsule; total cost over 12 months including the hours your team saves.
do_not: Do not match the price reflexively or disparage the competitor.
psychology: Price comparisons without scope comparisons are anchoring. Re-anchor on the outcome and the risk.

title: "Does it work with our Tally / ERP?"
trigger_description: A practical fit question about systems and data.
fact: Gong's 'concern' type: a minor, genuine question. Answer directly or bring in the right person; do not reframe.
impact: Concerns answered precisely build trust; concerns dodged become objections.
act: Good question, and I would rather answer it precisely than wave at it, because this is exactly where projects get stuck later. Tell me which system is your source of truth and what needs to flow in which direction, and I will tell you exactly what works today and what I need to confirm.
act_hinglish: Accha sawaal hai, aur main isko precisely answer karna chahunga, ghuma phira ke nahi, kyunki projects baad mein yahin atakte hain. Aap batayiye kaun sa system aapka source of truth hai aur kya data kis direction mein jaana chahiye, aur main exactly bataunga aaj kya chalta hai aur kya mujhe confirm karna hai.
question_to_ask: Do you want the two tools connected, or do you want to stop doing that task in the old tool altogether?
proof_point: Quote only integrations listed in the capsule; offer a technical call with a named person if it isn't listed.
do_not: Do not claim an integration that is not in your knowledge base.
psychology: Buyers test honesty with technical questions. A precise 'I'll confirm' beats a confident 'yes'.

title: Security, DPDP & compliance asks
trigger_description: Enterprise or finance buyers ask for security and compliance artefacts.
fact: Indian enterprise buyers expect SOC 2 Type II, SSO, RBAC, audit logs and 99.9% SLAs and ask for artefacts early; DPDP Rules obligations become enforceable on 13 May 2027.
impact: Deals die in security questionnaires and procurement queues nobody mapped. Treat it as paper process to be scheduled, not an objection to be argued.
act: That is exactly the right question to ask early, and I would rather we map your security review now so it runs alongside the evaluation instead of after it. Tell me who owns the vendor review on your side and I will get the right person from our team on a call with them.
act_hinglish: Yeh bilkul sahi sawaal hai, aur jaldi poochna accha hai. Main chahunga ki aapka security review abhi map kar lein taaki woh evaluation ke saath saath chale, baad mein nahi. Aap batayiye aapki side pe vendor review kaun handle karta hai, aur main hamari team ke sahi insaan ko unke saath call pe le aaunga.
question_to_ask: Who owns the vendor security review on your side, and how long does it usually take from start to sign-off?
proof_point: Share only the certifications and data-handling facts in the capsule; offer a security call with a named owner.
do_not: Do not guess at certifications or data locations you cannot verify.
psychology: Compliance asks are a condition of the deal. Mapping them early signals maturity.

title: "Just send me an email"
trigger_description: A polite exit disguised as a request for information.
fact: HubSpot: for brush-offs, ask one qualifying question and set a concrete next step; email without a follow-up date rarely converts.
impact: A deck sent into silence is a lost deal. One specific question keeps the conversation alive.
act: Happy to, and I will keep it short rather than sending you a forty-slide deck nobody reads. So that I send the right two pages, tell me the one thing you would want that email to answer, and let us put fifteen minutes on Thursday to go through it together.
act_hinglish: Bilkul, aur main isko chhota rakhunga, chaalis slide ka deck nahi bhejunga jo koi nahi padhta. Taaki main sahi do page bhej sakoon, aap batayiye woh ek cheez jo aap chahte hain email mein answer ho, aur Thursday ko pandrah minute rakh lete hain saath mein dekhne ke liye.
question_to_ask: If the email covers exactly that, can we book fifteen minutes on Thursday to go through it together?
proof_point: Send a WhatsApp summary plus a calendar invite within the hour, not a generic brochure.
do_not: Do not agree to 'send details' without a qualifying question and a follow-up date.
psychology: Brush-offs test whether you'll accept the exit. One relevant question signals you are worth 15 more minutes.

title: "Not a priority right now"
trigger_description: The problem is acknowledged but ranked below other work.
fact: Gong: feature-focused calls make a follow-up call significantly less likely; value topics (business impact, use cases) before next steps matter.
impact: Priority is set by cost of inaction. If the number isn't on the table, nothing you say reorders the list.
act: That is fair, you should only move on things that pay for themselves. Can I ask what the current approach is costing you each month, roughly, in hours or in rupees, because sometimes that number moves it up the list and sometimes it confirms it belongs lower down.
act_hinglish: Yeh fair hai, aapko sirf unhi cheezon pe move karna chahiye jo khud ko pay karein. Kya main pooch sakta hoon abhi ka tareeka aapko har mahine roughly kitna cost kar raha hai, ghanton mein ya rupaye mein, kyunki kabhi woh number isko list mein upar le aata hai aur kabhi confirm karta hai ki yeh neeche hi theek hai.
question_to_ask: What is the top priority for you right now, and does this problem slow that priority down in any way?
proof_point: Tie the outcome to their stated top priority rather than to your feature set.
do_not: Do not argue that it should be a priority; make the cost visible and let them conclude.
psychology: People reorder priorities when a cost becomes concrete and attributable, not when they are persuaded.

title: "I don't see the ROI"
trigger_description: The buyer cannot connect the spend to a number they own.
fact: MEDDPICC Metrics = the economic result the buyer is trying to move, stated as a number they own; Command of the Message requires a baseline and a target.
impact: ROI claims from the vendor are discounted; ROI calculated from the buyer's own numbers is believed.
act: Then let us build the return from your numbers rather than mine, because a vendor's ROI slide is not worth much. Tell me the baseline today, whether that is hours spent, follow-ups missed or receivable days, and we will put a realistic target next to it and see whether the maths works.
act_hinglish: Toh return aapke numbers se banate hain, mere nahi, kyunki vendor ki ROI slide ki koi value nahi hoti. Aap aaj ka baseline batayiye, chahe woh ghante hon, miss hue follow-ups hon ya receivable ke din, aur hum uske saamne ek realistic target rakhenge aur dekhenge maths banta hai ya nahi.
question_to_ask: If this saved your team eight hours a week, what would those hours go towards instead?
proof_point: A two-line baseline → target in INR per month agreed on the call and written into the follow-up.
do_not: Do not quote a generic ROI percentage or a case study with numbers they can't relate to.
psychology: Ownership of the metric creates commitment to the outcome.

title: "We don't want a long contract"
trigger_description: Commitment length is the concern.
fact: Gong (25,537 conversations): using risk-reversal language generously ('cancel any time', opt-outs, SLAs) correlated with a 32% win-rate lift; cancellations rose only about a point.
impact: Flexibility offered proactively is a strength; offered under pressure it looks like a concession.
act: I agree, you should not have to bet a whole year on us before we have proven anything. Let me explain the exit if it does not work out and what you get in return for committing once it does, and you can choose whichever structure feels safer for your business.
act_hinglish: Main agree karta hoon, humne kuch prove kiye bina aapko poora saal daav pe nahi lagana chahiye. Main bataata hoon agar kaam na bane toh exit kya hai, aur jab ban jaaye toh commit karne pe aapko kya milta hai, aur aap wahi structure chuniye jo aapke business ke liye safe lage.
question_to_ask: What would need to be true after sixty days for you to feel comfortable committing for the year?
proof_point: Only quote the terms the capsule allows (opt-out window, pilot-to-paid); trade annual prepay for a benefit, not a discount.
do_not: Do not invent cancellation terms or discounts you are not authorised to give.
psychology: Taking risk off the table (JOLT) addresses fear of messing up, which drives more lost deals than fear of missing out.

title: Pause after the objection
trigger_description: Any objection or concern: the first move is silence, not an answer.
fact: Gong (67,149 demos): top performers pause roughly 5x longer after an objection than average performers, and keep or slow their pace while average reps speed up.
impact: A fast, long answer signals anxiety and often answers the wrong objection. The pause buys the buyer room to say more.
act: Pause for two full seconds and let them finish completely. Then say: That is a fair concern, and I would rather understand it properly than give you a quick answer. Tell me a bit more about what is behind it, and then I will respond to the actual issue.
act_hinglish: Do second poori tarah rukiye aur unhe poora bolne dijiye. Phir kahiye: Yeh fair concern hai, aur main jaldi jawab dene se pehle isko theek se samajhna chahunga. Thoda aur batayiye iske peeche kya hai, phir main asli issue pe jawab dunga.
question_to_ask: What is behind that concern for you, is it something you have seen go wrong before?
proof_point: Keep the eventual answer under 20 words and end it with a question.
do_not: Do not interrupt, speed up, or launch a 20-second monologue.
psychology: Silence after an objection is read as confidence; the buyer usually fills it with the real reason.

title: Isolate before you answer
trigger_description: The prospect states one objection; check whether it is the only one before answering.
fact: Gong's smokescreen handling: assume the stated objection is solved and ask what else stands in the way before answering.
impact: Answering a smokescreen wins an argument and loses the deal; isolating reveals the real blocker.
act: Let me make sure I answer the right thing. Suppose we solved that completely and it was no longer a concern at all. Would there be anything else we would need to get right before you felt comfortable moving ahead, or is that genuinely the one thing?
act_hinglish: Main pakka karna chahta hoon ki sahi cheez ka jawab doon. Maan lijiye hum isko poori tarah solve kar dein aur yeh concern bilkul na rahe. Kya phir bhi kuch aur hoga jo humein theek karna padega aage badhne ke liye, ya sach mein yahi ek cheez hai?
question_to_ask: Is that the main thing holding you back, or is there something behind it that we have not talked about yet?
proof_point: Write the full list of blockers back to the buyer before addressing the first one.
do_not: Do not answer the first objection in full before you know whether it is the only one.
psychology: Stated objections are often labels for a deeper concern; exploration before response is the pivotal step (LAER).

title: Take risk off the table
trigger_description: The buyer voices fear of making a wrong decision.
fact: JOLT: fear of messing up (FOMU) drives more lost deals than fear of missing out; escalating with fear or discounts increased loss likelihood in 84% of such interactions. Gong: risk-reversal language +32% win rate.
impact: Reassurance plus a concrete safety net moves indecisive buyers; pressure does the opposite.
act: That is a reasonable worry, and I would rather make this safe to try than ask you to trust me. We can run a defined pilot with a success metric you choose, a date on which we both decide, and a clear exit if it does not hit the number. That way the risk sits with us, not with you.
act_hinglish: Yeh reasonable worry hai, aur main chahta hoon yeh try karna safe ho, aap mujhpe bharosa karein yeh zaroori nahi. Hum ek defined pilot kar sakte hain jisme success metric aap chunein, ek date jisme hum dono decide karein, aur agar number na aaye toh clear exit. Is tarah risk hamare paas rehta hai, aapke paas nahi.
question_to_ask: What would 'it worked' look like to you in numbers by the end of a pilot?
proof_point: Only the opt-out, SLA and pilot terms your company actually offers (from the capsule).
do_not: Do not create urgency with fake deadlines or a sudden discount.
psychology: Reducing downside risk is more persuasive to indecisive buyers than increasing the upside.

title: Why we win (template)
trigger_description: The buyer asks what makes you different; answer with one or two reasons tied to their criteria.
fact: Klue sources Why We Win content by interviewing the sellers who won the last ten deals against each competitor; quality principles are Context (the 'so what'), Charge and Specificity.
impact: A generic differentiator list is forgotten; one reason that maps to the buyer's own decision criterion is repeated internally.
act: I could give you a list, but you would forget it by tomorrow. Customers who chose us over the alternative usually did so for one reason, the one that maps to what you said matters most. Let me explain that one properly, and you tell me whether it is a real differentiator for your situation.
act_hinglish: Main ek list de sakta hoon, lekin aap kal tak bhool jaayenge. Jin customers ne humein alternative ke bajaye chuna, unhone usually ek wajah se chuna, aur wahi wajah hai jo aapke liye sabse important cheez se match karti hai. Main wahi ek baat theek se samjhata hoon, aur aap batayiye aapki situation mein yeh sach mein fark karti hai ya nahi.
question_to_ask: Of everything you have listed, which two criteria would decide it for you if everything else were equal?
proof_point: Use the key differentiators from the product capsule verbatim; add a reference deal if one exists.
do_not: Do not list more than two differentiators; do not mention competitor weaknesses you cannot prove.
psychology: Specific, charged, contextual claims are believed; neutral feature parity is ignored.

title: Why we lose / go-no-go
trigger_description: The buyer states a requirement you may not meet; decide whether to engage.
fact: Klue's 'Why We Lose' doubles as a Go/No-Go rule set drawn from win-loss analysis; keeping cards current is 'the most important step'.
impact: Chasing a deal you structurally lose costs the time that wins the next one. Saying so early builds credibility.
act: I will be straight with you, because it saves us both time. If that requirement is a genuine must-have from day one, we may not be your best fit yet, and I would rather tell you now than find out in month three. If it is important but not day-one critical, then there is a conversation worth having.
act_hinglish: Main seedhi baat karunga, kyunki isse hum dono ka time bachta hai. Agar yeh requirement pehle din se sach mein must-have hai, toh shayad hum abhi aapke liye best fit nahi hain, aur main yeh abhi bata dena chahta hoon, teesre mahine pata chalne se accha. Agar yeh important hai lekin pehle din zaroori nahi, toh baat karne layak hai.
question_to_ask: If that requirement were met six months from now, would the rest of this still be worth doing today?
proof_point: The capsule's roadmap or scope statement; never a promise of a feature date.
do_not: Do not promise unbuilt features to stay in the deal.
psychology: Honest disqualification raises trust and often converts a 'must-have' into a negotiable.

title: Landmines to lay
trigger_description: A competitive evaluation is under way; plant the questions competitors answer badly.
fact: Klue: landmines are questions or claims a rep plants that the competitor cannot answer well; objections 'typically come from landmines a competitor has laid'. Gong: raising competitors early helps, late hurts.
impact: The buyer carries your questions into the competitor's demo. Plant them now, not after the shortlist.
act: Since you are comparing, ask every vendor the same three things so it is fair. Ask how they handle the exact problem you described to me, what the total cost looks like after month one, and what happens to your data and support if you ever want to leave. I will put those in writing for you.
act_hinglish: Kyunki aap compare kar rahe hain, main suggest karunga har vendor se same teen cheezein poochiye taaki comparison fair ho. Poochiye woh aapki batayi hui exact problem kaise handle karte hain, pehle mahine ke baad total cost kaisa dikhta hai, aur agar aap kabhi chhodna chahein toh aapke data aur support ka kya hota hai. Main yeh teen sawaal likh ke bhej dunga.
question_to_ask: What are the other vendors telling you is the most important thing to evaluate?
proof_point: Three evaluation questions written into the follow-up email so they travel to the next demo.
do_not: Do not name the competitor's weaknesses directly; ask the questions that expose them.
psychology: Buyers trust criteria they believe they chose themselves.

title: Promoter / founder sign-off
trigger_description: An owner-led business where the promoter approves spend regardless of ticket size.
fact: Practitioner guidance: many Indian SME purchases require founder approval regardless of price; decision-making is relationship-driven, not just ROI-driven. Promoters fear vendor dependency and loss of personal control.
impact: Your contact is almost never the economic buyer. The deal closes in a meeting you are not in unless you ask to join it.
act: In most businesses like yours the owner wants to see something like this personally before saying yes, and that is completely reasonable. Could we set up a short twenty-minute walkthrough with them, where I keep it to cash impact and what stays in their control, and skip the feature tour entirely?
act_hinglish: Aapke jaise zyada tar businesses mein owner haan bolne se pehle aisi cheez khud dekhna chahte hain, aur yeh bilkul reasonable hai. Kya hum unke saath ek chhota bees minute ka walkthrough rakh sakte hain, jisme main sirf cash impact aur unke control mein kya rehta hai pe baat karoon, features ka tour bilkul nahi?
question_to_ask: When the MD evaluates a new system, what do they want to be sure of first: the cost, the control, or who else is already using it?
proof_point: A one-page promoter summary: outcome in cash terms, phased rollout, exit terms, and what stays under their control.
do_not: Do not treat the manager on the call as the final decision-maker.
psychology: Promoters treat technology as a structural commitment; reduce perceived dependency and loss of control.

title: The CA / finance gate
trigger_description: The chartered accountant or finance team must approve the vendor and the invoicing.
fact: Atradius: operational frictions (approval and banking delays) are a main cause of late payment in India; the paper process includes PO raising, vendor registration and GST invoice acceptance.
impact: A CA who was not consulted can stall payment for months. A CA who was briefed becomes an ally.
act: Let us make your CA's job easy from the start, because that is where good deals get stuck for months. I will send one page with the GST-compliant invoice format, the HSN or SAC code, the TDS treatment and our vendor registration details, so their questions are answered before they ask them.
act_hinglish: Shuru se hi aapke CA ka kaam easy kar dete hain, kyunki acchi deals wahin mahinon tak atak jaati hain. Main ek page bhej dunga jisme GST compliant invoice format, HSN ya SAC code, TDS treatment aur hamari vendor registration details hongi, taaki unke sawaal poochne se pehle hi answer ho jaayein.
question_to_ask: Does your accounts team need a PO before any invoice, and what is the usual approval chain on your side?
proof_point: A CA-facing one-pager with GST-inclusive and exclusive pricing and payment options (UPI AutoPay, NACH).
do_not: Do not skip the finance stakeholder because the business owner said yes.
psychology: Finance gatekeepers reward vendors who reduce their compliance effort.

title: Working-capital lens
trigger_description: The buyer thinks in cash terms: receivables, inventory, collections.
fact: Indian promoters ask whether an investment reduces working capital 'or just increases reporting' and judge success by faster decisions and tighter working capital.
impact: Dashboards do not sell to promoters; cash does. Translate every outcome into receivable days, inventory or hours.
act: Let us measure this the way you actually run the business, not the way a software company would. Either it brings cash in faster or it frees up your people's time, and if it does neither then it is just more reporting. Tell me which of those two matters more this quarter and we will focus only on that.
act_hinglish: Isko waise measure karte hain jaise aap business chalaate hain, software company ke tareeke se nahi. Ya toh yeh paisa jaldi laata hai ya aapke logon ka time bachaata hai, aur agar dono nahi karta toh yeh sirf extra reporting hai. Batayiye is quarter mein in dono mein kya zyada matter karta hai, aur hum sirf uspe focus karenge.
question_to_ask: How many days of receivables are outstanding today, and what would five fewer days be worth to you?
proof_point: An outcome stated in INR per month or days-sales-outstanding, from their own numbers.
do_not: Do not sell reporting, visibility or dashboards as the headline benefit.
psychology: Owner-operators optimise for cash and control; reframe benefits in those two currencies.

title: The negotiation ritual
trigger_description: The buyer asks for a discount as a matter of course.
fact: Practitioners budget for a 20–30% negotiation on almost every Indian deal; discount pressure is a ritual, not a verdict. JOLT: discounting in response to hesitation increases loss likelihood.
impact: An instant discount teaches the buyer the price was padded. Trading a concession for something keeps the price credible.
act: I would rather trade than cut, because if I simply drop the price you will rightly wonder what else was padded. If we go annual, if you are open to being a reference, or if we tighten the scope, I can do something meaningful for you. Tell me which of those works and I will put a number to it.
act_hinglish: Main kaatne ki bajaye trade karna chahunga, kyunki agar main bas price gira doon toh aap sochenge aur kya padded tha. Agar hum annual karein, aap reference banne ke liye open hain, ya hum scope thoda tight karein, toh main aapke liye kuch meaningful kar sakta hoon. Batayiye inme se kya chalega aur main uspe number lagaata hoon.
question_to_ask: Is the ask about the total number, or about how it is structured across the year?
proof_point: Only the trade-offs your pricing policy allows (annual prepay, case study, referral, scope).
do_not: Do not drop the price in response to silence or a frown.
psychology: Reciprocity: a concession earned feels fair; a concession given feels like a hidden margin.

title: Payment terms & collections
trigger_description: The buyer asks for credit terms or delayed payment.
fact: Atradius 2026: Indian B2B payment terms are typically 1–2 months; nearly nine in ten firms report overdue invoices; outstanding payments exceed a third of receivables.
impact: Collections risk is part of deal design. Terms agreed loosely on the call become disputes at invoice time.
act: Let us design the payment so it is easy on both sides and nobody is chasing anyone later. We can do annual or quarterly through UPI AutoPay or NACH, and if there is a services piece we can bill on milestones. Tell me how your approvals usually work and I will fit the schedule to that.
act_hinglish: Payment ko aise design karte hain ki dono side ke liye easy ho aur baad mein koi kisi ke peeche na bhaage. Hum annual ya quarterly UPI AutoPay ya NACH se kar sakte hain, aur agar services ka hissa hai toh milestones pe bill kar sakte hain. Batayiye aapke approvals usually kaise chalte hain, main schedule usi hisaab se bana dunga.
question_to_ask: How does your company usually pay software vendors: in advance, monthly, or against a PO?
proof_point: Offer the payment options in the capsule; put the terms in the follow-up email.
do_not: Do not agree to open-ended credit to win the signature.
psychology: Clarity on payment removes a hidden source of post-sale friction and signals a professional vendor.

title: PoC fatigue: scope the pilot
trigger_description: The buyer asks for a free trial or PoC, possibly after others.
fact: Indian customers almost always expect a free trial; founders report stopping India sales after 'PoCs after PoCs'. Customers pay when they feel they are missing revenue or an opportunity.
impact: An unscoped PoC never ends. A pilot with a metric, a date and a price-on-success is a sales step.
act: Happy to run a pilot, that is a sensible way to decide. Let us agree three things before we start though: what it worked means in actual numbers, the date on which we sit down and decide, and what happens when it hits the number. That way the pilot is a decision, not an open-ended trial.
act_hinglish: Pilot zaroor karte hain, decide karne ka yeh sahi tareeka hai. Lekin start karne se pehle teen cheezein tay kar lete hain: kaam ban gaya ka matlab actual numbers mein kya hai, woh date jisme hum baith ke decide karenge, aur jab number aa jaaye toh kya hoga. Is tarah pilot ek decision hoga, open-ended trial nahi.
question_to_ask: If the pilot hits the number we agree on, is there anything else that would stop you from going ahead?
proof_point: A one-paragraph pilot charter: scope, success metric, decision date, price on success.
do_not: Do not start a free trial without a success metric and a decision date.
psychology: A defined pilot converts curiosity into commitment; an open PoC converts it into free consulting.

title: Trust deficit from past vendors
trigger_description: A bad past vendor experience is driving hesitation.
fact: Indian companies are described as cautious buyers due to past negative experiences rather than price; remedies named are references, clear pilot results and consistent support.
impact: Trust is rebuilt with specifics the buyer can verify, not with assurances.
act: That experience is exactly why I would set this up differently from day one. You would have a named support person whose number you keep, a reference in your city you can call before you sign anything, and a clear exit if we do not deliver what we said. I would rather earn the trust than ask for it.
act_hinglish: Woh experience hi wajah hai ki main isko pehle din se alag tareeke se set karunga. Aapke paas ek named support person hoga jiska number aapke paas rahega, aapke city mein ek reference jisko aap sign karne se pehle call kar sakte hain, aur agar hum jo kaha woh na dein toh clear exit. Main trust maangne ki bajaye kamaana chahunga.
question_to_ask: What did support look like with the last vendor by month three, and what would you want to be different this time?
proof_point: A same-city or same-industry reference plus the support SLA from the capsule.
do_not: Do not say 'that won't happen with us' without something verifiable behind it.
psychology: Risk reversal and local social proof address the fear of being burnt again.

title: FY-end and festive timing
trigger_description: The buyer references the Indian financial year or festive calendar.
fact: March marks the end of India's financial year with targets to meet and budgets resetting in April; pre-Diwali is a stock-building, cash-tight period for traders and manufacturers.
impact: These cycles are natural deadlines and natural stalls. Use them as a plan, not an excuse.
act: That is a real consideration and we should plan around it rather than pretend it is not there. The question is whether you want this live before the thirty-first of March so it sits in this year's budget, or whether we lock the pricing now and go live in April with nothing landing on your team during the busy period.
act_hinglish: Yeh ek real baat hai aur humein iske hisaab se plan karna chahiye, ignore nahi. Sawaal yeh hai ki aap isko ikattis March se pehle live chahte hain taaki yeh is saal ke budget mein aa jaaye, ya hum pricing abhi lock karein aur April mein live karein, taaki busy season mein aapki team pe kuch na pade.
question_to_ask: What does the next festive season look like for your volumes, and what would you want working before it starts?
proof_point: A mutual action plan that works backwards from the buyer's own deadline.
do_not: Do not accept 'after Diwali' without a specific week and an owner.
psychology: External deadlines feel legitimate to buyers; attach the decision to one they already respect.

title: Mirror the buyer's language mix
trigger_description: The buyer code-switches into Hindi or Hinglish.
fact: Only about 10% of India is English-proficient; code-mixing is treated as a naturalness requirement for conversational AI and as a trust signal in sales conversations.
impact: Matching the buyer's register lowers friction; jargon in formal English raises it.
act: Switch your next lines to the buyer's mix and drop the jargon. For example: Bilkul, samajh gaya, toh abhi jo follow-up ka kaam hai woh kaun handle karta hai, aur jab woh busy hote hain toh kya hota hai? Keep product names and numbers exact in either language.
act_hinglish: Apni agli lines buyer ke mix mein boliye aur jargon hata dijiye. Jaise: Bilkul, samajh gaya, toh abhi jo follow-up ka kaam hai woh kaun handle karta hai, aur jab woh busy hote hain toh kya hota hai? Product ke naam aur numbers dono bhasha mein exact rakhiye.
question_to_ask: Aapke yahan abhi yeh process kaise chalta hai, aur kahan sabse zyada time lagta hai?
proof_point: Keep product names and numbers exact in either language; mirror tone, not slang.
do_not: Do not over-correct into heavy Hindi or imitate regional slang you don't use naturally.
psychology: Linguistic mirroring signals in-group membership and lowers perceived sales pressure.

title: GST framing of the price
trigger_description: Tax treatment of the quote is unclear or disputed.
fact: SaaS in India attracts 18% GST; registered businesses can usually claim input tax credit, so the effective cost differs from the sticker price.
impact: An ambiguous 'plus taxes' quote becomes a 18% surprise at invoice time and a reason to stall.
act: Let me be exact about the tax so there is no surprise later. The price I quoted is before GST, so eighteen percent gets added on the invoice, and if your business is GST registered you claim that back as input credit, which means your effective cost is the base price. I will write both figures in the follow-up.
act_hinglish: Tax ke baare mein exact bata deta hoon taaki baad mein koi surprise na ho. Jo price maine bataya woh GST se pehle hai, toh invoice pe atharah percent add hoga, aur agar aapka business GST registered hai toh aap woh input credit ke roop mein wapas claim karte hain, matlab aapka effective cost base price hi hai. Main dono figures follow-up mein likh dunga.
question_to_ask: Is your business GST registered, so that we can show you the effective cost after input credit?
proof_point: Quote both inclusive and exclusive figures from the capsule price; never compute a new price on the fly.
do_not: Do not quote 'plus taxes' without the number; do not invent the price.
psychology: Transparency on tax signals competence and removes a late-stage friction point.

title: WhatsApp is the follow-up channel
trigger_description: The buyer prefers WhatsApp over email for follow-ups.
fact: WhatsApp is described as the default Indian SMB channel; a wa.me click-to-chat recap from the rep's own number costs nothing and needs no template approval.
impact: An email recap may go unread for days; a WhatsApp summary with the next step is read within the hour.
act: I will send you a short WhatsApp summary within the hour, with the three things we agreed and the time for our next conversation, nothing longer than that. Just confirm this is the right number for you, and let me know if anyone else on your side should get the same message.
act_hinglish: Main ek ghante ke andar WhatsApp pe chhota summary bhej dunga, jisme humne jo teen cheezein tay ki aur agli baat ka time hoga, usse zyada kuch nahi. Bas confirm kar dijiye yeh sahi number hai, aur batayiye aapki side pe kisi aur ko bhi yahi message jaana chahiye ya nahi.
question_to_ask: Should I also send the summary to anyone else on your side, so everyone has the same picture?
proof_point: Keep the recap under 90 words: outcome, next step with date, one link.
do_not: Do not send the full deck or a long message on WhatsApp.
psychology: A fast, short recap on the buyer's preferred channel reinforces commitment while memory is fresh.

title: Metrics: a number they own
trigger_description: Discovery without a quantified outcome; or the buyer mentions a number in passing.
fact: Metrics = the economic result the buyer is trying to move, stated as a number they own; Command of the Message needs a baseline and a target.
impact: Deals without a buyer-owned metric are decided on price; deals with one are decided on value.
act: Can I put a rough number on that with you, because it will matter later when you justify this internally? Roughly what does that cost you today each month, either in rupees or in people's hours, and let us write that down as the baseline we are trying to move.
act_hinglish: Kya main aapke saath ispe ek rough number laga sakta hoon, kyunki baad mein jab aap isko internally justify karenge tab yeh matter karega? Roughly yeh aaj aapko har mahine kitna cost karta hai, rupaye mein ya logon ke ghanton mein, aur isko hum baseline ke roop mein likh lete hain jisko humein badalna hai.
question_to_ask: If this were fixed, what would be different for you by the end of the quarter, in numbers?
proof_point: Repeat the baseline and target back in the follow-up email.
do_not: Do not supply the metric yourself; the buyer must own it.
psychology: A number the buyer states becomes a commitment they defend internally.

title: Economic buyer
trigger_description: The economic buyer has not been identified or named.
fact: The Economic Buyer has final budget authority and can approve even if others object; a champion sells internally while the economic buyer signs the cheque.
impact: Single-threaded below the economic buyer is the most common reason Indian SME deals stall at the promoter.
act: So that I plan the next steps properly and do not waste your time, help me understand how a decision like this gets made here. Who ultimately signs off on a spend of this size, and have they bought something similar before, so I know what they will want to see?
act_hinglish: Taaki main agle steps theek se plan karoon aur aapka time na waste ho, mujhe samjhaiye yahan aisa decision kaise hota hai. Is size ke kharche pe final sign off kaun karta hai, aur kya unhone pehle aisa kuch kharida hai, taaki mujhe pata ho woh kya dekhna chahenge?
question_to_ask: How did the last system you bought get approved: who said yes, and who had to be convinced along the way?
proof_point: Name the EB in the deal record; propose a meeting with them as the next step.
do_not: Do not assume the enthusiastic contact is the buyer.
psychology: Buyers reveal the real approver when asked about past purchases rather than about themselves.

title: Decision criteria
trigger_description: What the buyer will judge on is unclear or shaped by a competitor.
fact: Decision Criteria map to Command of the Message's Required Capabilities; criteria shaped by a competitor are a live risk signal.
impact: If you don't know the criteria, you are being evaluated on someone else's.
act: Before I show you anything, I want to understand what you will actually judge this on, because otherwise I will guess and probably guess wrong. What must any solution do for you to pick it, and of those things, which one or two are genuinely non-negotiable rather than nice to have?
act_hinglish: Kuch dikhane se pehle main samajhna chahta hoon aap isko actually kis cheez pe judge karenge, warna main andaaza lagaunga aur shayad galat lagaunga. Koi bhi solution kya zaroor kare tabhi aap usko chunenge, aur unme se kaun si ek ya do cheezein sach mein non-negotiable hain, nice to have nahi?
question_to_ask: Where did that list of requirements come from: your own team, a consultant, or another vendor's demo?
proof_point: Restate the criteria in the follow-up and map each to a capsule capability.
do_not: Do not accept a vague 'ease of use' without asking what it means for them.
psychology: Buyers who articulate their criteria out loud become more consistent in applying them.

title: Decision process
trigger_description: The path from today to a signed decision is undefined.
fact: Vague 'we'll discuss internally' is the live watch-for; the fill question is 'walk me through how you bought your last system'.
impact: Without a mapped process, every next step is a guess and every stall a surprise.
act: It would help me a lot to understand how decisions like this normally run here, so I can fit into your process rather than push my own. Walk me through how you bought your last system, who was involved, how long it took, and where it got stuck, and I will plan around that.
act_hinglish: Mujhe bahut help hogi agar main samajh loon ki yahan aise decisions normally kaise chalte hain, taaki main apna process thopne ki bajaye aapke process mein fit ho sakoon. Mujhe batayiye aapne pichla system kaise kharida, kaun involved tha, kitna time laga, aur kahan atka, aur main usi hisaab se plan karunga.
question_to_ask: What has to happen between today and a yes, and who owns each of those steps on your side?
proof_point: A mutual action plan with the steps the buyer described, dated.
do_not: Do not accept 'we'll get back to you' as a process.
psychology: Asking about the past purchase feels safe and reveals the real process.

title: Paper process
trigger_description: Contracting, procurement and compliance steps have not been mapped.
fact: Deals have died in a security questionnaire or a procurement queue nobody had mapped; in India the paper process includes PO raising, vendor registration, GST invoice acceptance and the payment-approval chain.
impact: Paper process is the most common cause of a 'verbal yes' that takes three months to invoice.
act: One practical thing while we are here, because this is where good decisions get stuck for months. Are there any vendor onboarding, security review, PO or GST steps on your side that we should start in parallel now, so they do not hold things up once you have decided?
act_hinglish: Ek practical baat abhi kar lete hain, kyunki acche decisions yahin mahinon tak atak jaate hain. Kya aapki side pe koi vendor onboarding, security review, PO ya GST ke steps hain jo humein abhi parallel mein shuru kar dene chahiye, taaki decide hone ke baad woh cheezein na rokein?
question_to_ask: Who raises the PO on your side, and how long does vendor registration usually take with your accounts team?
proof_point: Send the vendor registration documents proactively once the fit is confirmed.
do_not: Do not raise paper process on a first discovery call before pain is established.
psychology: Mapping paperwork early signals you have done this before.

title: Identify (and implicate) the pain
trigger_description: The buyer hints at a problem; go deeper before pitching.
fact: Gong: successful discovery calls dive deeply into 3–4 problems; beyond four each seems less urgent. Sandler's pain funnel moves from surface frustration to business and personal consequence.
impact: A pain stated once is forgotten; a pain explored to its consequence becomes the reason to buy.
act: Tell me more about that, because it sounds like more than a small irritation. How long has it been going on, what have you already tried to fix it, and what actually happens to the business when it goes wrong, not in theory but the last time it happened?
act_hinglish: Iske baare mein thoda aur batayiye, kyunki yeh chhoti pareshaani se zyada lagta hai. Yeh kab se chal raha hai, aapne isko fix karne ke liye ab tak kya try kiya, aur jab yeh galat hota hai toh business pe actually kya asar hota hai, theory mein nahi, pichli baar jab hua tha?
question_to_ask: What does that cost you when it happens, and how does it land on you personally?
proof_point: Write the pain in the buyer's words into the brief and the follow-up.
do_not: Do not jump to the solution at the first mention of a problem.
psychology: Implication questions raise the perceived cost of the problem before any price is discussed.

title: Champion
trigger_description: Someone shows personal stake; test and equip them as a champion.
fact: A Champion has organisational power, access to the economic buyer and a personal stake; single-threading after call 2 is the live risk signal.
impact: A champion sells when you're not in the room; a fan merely agrees when you are.
act: That is good to hear, and I want to make it easy for you to carry this internally rather than leaving you exposed. Tell me what you would need from me to make the case in a way that works here, and who else would push for this if you were out of office for a month.
act_hinglish: Yeh sunke accha laga, aur main chahta hoon ki aapke liye isko internally aage le jaana easy ho, aap akele exposed na rahein. Batayiye mujhse aapko kya chahiye taaki yahan ke hisaab se case bana sakein, aur agar aap ek mahine office se bahar hote toh aur kaun isko push karta.
question_to_ask: What does this do for you personally if it works the way we have discussed?
proof_point: Give the champion a one-page internal case in their own words.
do_not: Do not confuse enthusiasm with influence; test access to the economic buyer.
psychology: People champion what makes them look good internally.

title: Competition incl. doing nothing
trigger_description: Alternatives, including the status quo, have not been surfaced.
fact: The MEDDPICC question is 'What other approaches are you evaluating?'; Gong finds competitors raised early help and raised late hurt.
impact: The alternative you don't know about is the one you lose to.
act: I would rather know this now than find out later. What else are you considering for this, including doing nothing for another six months or handling it with your own team, because each of those has a real cost and I would like to compare honestly against all of them.
act_hinglish: Main yeh abhi jaanna chahunga, baad mein pata chalne se accha. Iske liye aap aur kya consider kar rahe hain, including agle chhe mahine kuch na karna ya apni team se handle karna, kyunki har option ki ek real cost hai aur main un sab ke saamne honestly compare karna chahunga.
question_to_ask: If you did nothing about this for six months, what would that cost the business?
proof_point: Record every alternative, including Excel/Tally and in-house, in the deal record.
do_not: Do not wait for the buyer to raise the competitor.
psychology: Naming the status quo as a competitor makes its cost discussable.

title: Budget: raise it on call 1
trigger_description: Budget has not been discussed and the call is past the halfway mark.
fact: Gong: budget discussed on call 1 correlated with a 49% win rate vs 7% when never discussed; star reps raise price in the last quarter of the call.
impact: Avoiding budget on the first call does not protect the deal; it removes the information that qualifies it.
act: Before we go much further, can I ask about budget, not to pin you down but so I recommend the right size of solution? Is there money set aside for something like this, or would it come out of this year's operating spend and need someone's approval?
act_hinglish: Aage badhne se pehle, kya main budget ke baare mein pooch sakta hoon, aapko pin karne ke liye nahi, balki sahi size ka solution recommend karne ke liye? Kya aisi cheez ke liye paisa alag rakha hai, ya yeh is saal ke operating spend se aayega aur kisi ka approval chahiye hoga?
question_to_ask: What range were you expecting for a solution like this, roughly?
proof_point: Quote the capsule price with GST clarity when asked; never a made-up range.
do_not: Do not open the call with price, and do not end it without having discussed budget.
psychology: Budget conversations feel safe when framed as sourcing ('where would it come from') rather than as a demand.

title: Authority
trigger_description: Who can say yes is unclear.
fact: BANT's Authority maps to the MEDDPICC Economic Buyer; HubSpot's authority objections include 'not authorised' and 'can't sell internally'.
impact: A deal sold to the wrong level restarts at the right one.
act: Just so I plan the next conversation with the right people, besides yourself, who else would need to be comfortable with this before it goes ahead? I ask because in most companies there is a finance person or a partner who sees it at the end, and I would rather include them early.
act_hinglish: Bas taaki main agli baat sahi logon ke saath plan karoon, aapke alawa aur kaun hai jisko aage badhne se pehle comfortable hona chahiye? Main isliye pooch raha hoon kyunki zyada tar companies mein ek finance wala ya partner hota hai jo end mein dekhta hai, aur main unhe jaldi include karna chahunga.
question_to_ask: If you were fully convinced today, what would happen next on your side, and who would be involved?
proof_point: Propose including the approver on the next call invite.
do_not: Do not ask 'are you the decision maker?'; it invites a face-saving yes.
psychology: Indirect authority questions get honest answers; direct ones get defensive ones.

title: Need: the real one
trigger_description: A stated need that has not been connected to a business consequence.
fact: Gap Selling: uncover current state (environment, problem, impact, root cause, emotion) and the desired future state; spend about a quarter of the cycle on discovery.
impact: A feature-level need ('we need WhatsApp automation') hides the business need ('we lose leads overnight').
act: That is clear, and before I take that at face value I want to understand what is behind it. What is happening today that made this a need rather than a wish, and if it were solved properly, what would be different for the business, not for the software but for the business?
act_hinglish: Yeh clear hai, aur isko seedha maan lene se pehle main samajhna chahta hoon iske peeche kya hai. Aaj aisa kya ho raha hai jisne isko wish se zaroorat bana diya, aur agar yeh theek se solve ho jaaye toh business ke liye kya alag hoga, software ke liye nahi, business ke liye?
question_to_ask: What have you already tried to solve this, and why did it not stick?
proof_point: Restate the need as a business outcome in the follow-up.
do_not: Do not accept a feature request as the need.
psychology: Needs stated as outcomes survive the internal debate; needs stated as features get compared on price.

title: Timeline
trigger_description: No target date for the outcome exists.
fact: Committed buyers raise start dates and implementation questions unprompted; their absence is a heuristic warning sign.
impact: A deal without a buyer-owned date has no reason to close this quarter.
act: Let me ask about timing from your side rather than mine. When do you actually need this working, and is there something driving that date, like the financial year end, a new branch, a hire or the festive season? If there is nothing driving it, that is useful to know too.
act_hinglish: Timing ke baare mein aapki side se poochta hoon, meri side se nahi. Aapko yeh actually kab tak chalta hua chahiye, aur kya us date ke peeche kuch hai, jaise financial year end, nayi branch, koi hiring ya festive season? Agar kuch nahi hai toh woh bhi jaanna useful hai.
question_to_ask: What happens on your side if this is not working by that date?
proof_point: Work backwards from the date in a mutual action plan.
do_not: Do not impose your quarter-end as their deadline.
psychology: Dates tied to the buyer's own events are kept; dates tied to the vendor's are not.

title: Need-payoff questions
trigger_description: The buyer imagines a better state; let them articulate the value.
fact: SPIN's need-payoff questions get the buyer to state the value of a solution themselves, which reduces objections later.
impact: Value the buyer articulates is value they will defend internally.
act: Let us stay with that for a second, because it sounds like the thing that actually matters. If that were handled automatically from next month, what would it free up for you and your team, and who in the business would notice the difference first?
act_hinglish: Ek second ispe rukte hain, kyunki yahi woh cheez lagti hai jo actually matter karti hai. Agar yeh agle mahine se automatically handle ho jaaye, toh aapke aur aapki team ke liye kya free hoga, aur business mein sabse pehle fark kaun notice karega?
question_to_ask: How would you explain that benefit to your MD in a single sentence?
proof_point: Use the buyer's own need-payoff sentence as the opening line of the follow-up email.
do_not: Do not answer your own need-payoff question with your pitch.
psychology: Self-generated arguments are more persuasive than received ones.

title: Open with an up-front contract
trigger_description: The first two minutes of the call.
fact: Sandler's Up-Front Contract agrees purpose, both agendas, time and possible outcomes at the start, including that 'no' is an acceptable outcome.
impact: Fixing the agenda and the next-step decision up front prevents the call ending in 'send me an email'.
act: Thanks for the time. We have about thirty minutes, so here is what I would suggest: I would like to understand how you handle this today, show you one thing that is relevant and nothing more, and by the end agree whether a next step makes sense, and no is a perfectly fine answer. Does that work for you?
act_hinglish: Time ke liye shukriya. Hamare paas tees minute hain, toh main yeh suggest karunga: main samajhna chahunga aap aaj isko kaise handle karte hain, aapko ek relevant cheez dikhaunga aur usse zyada kuch nahi, aur end mein tay karenge ki agla step banta hai ya nahi, aur nahi bhi bilkul theek jawab hai. Chalega?
question_to_ask: What would make this a genuinely good use of your thirty minutes today?
proof_point: Name the decision you'll ask for at the end (a dated next step) before discovery starts.
do_not: Do not open with the company story or a demo.
psychology: Agreed outcomes up front make the closing question expected rather than pushy.

title: Discovery: 3–4 problems, spread the questions
trigger_description: The buyer describes their current process.
fact: Gong (519,291 conversations): successful discovery calls explore 3–4 problems and spread questions through the call; 2025 data shows won deals with 15–16 questions vs ~20 in lost deals.
impact: Front-loading questions feels like an interrogation; more than four problems dilutes urgency.
act: That is really useful, thank you. Of the things you have just described, one of them sounded like it frustrates you more than the others, so rather than running through a list of questions, I would like to go one level deeper on that one and understand what actually happens when it goes wrong.
act_hinglish: Yeh bahut useful hai, shukriya. Jo cheezein aapne abhi batayi, unme se ek aisi lagi jo aapko baaki se zyada frustrate karti hai, toh sawaalon ki list chalaane ki bajaye main usi ek pe ek level aur neeche jaana chahunga aur samajhna chahunga jab woh galat hota hai toh actually kya hota hai.
question_to_ask: Of everything you have mentioned, which one costs you the most sleep?
proof_point: Record the top problems in the buyer's words with a cost each.
do_not: Do not run a checklist of questions in the first ten minutes.
psychology: Depth on a few problems builds the case; breadth across many flattens it.

title: Demo: tie every feature to a stated problem
trigger_description: The demo begins or the buyer asks to see something.
fact: Gong: successful early demos are about twice as interactive (speaker switches) as unsuccessful ones; feature-dumping cuts win rates from 26% to 5%.
impact: A demo is a conversation with a screen in it, not a tour.
act: Rather than give you the full tour, let me show only the part that matches what you told me, which was follow-ups slipping when the team gets busy. I will walk through that one workflow, and then I want you to tell me whether it matches how your people would actually use it or whether I have missed something.
act_hinglish: Poora tour dene ki bajaye, main sirf wahi hissa dikhaata hoon jo aapki batayi baat se match karta hai, yaani team busy hone pe follow-ups chhoot jaana. Main woh ek workflow dikhaunga, aur phir aap batayiye ki yeh aapke log actually aise use karenge ya maine kuch miss kiya.
question_to_ask: Who on your team would be doing this step day to day, and what would they find awkward about it?
proof_point: Show at most three workflows, each introduced with the buyer's own problem statement.
do_not: Do not show features nobody asked about.
psychology: Buyers evaluate relevance, not completeness.

title: Pricing: recap value, then the number
trigger_description: The buyer asks for the price or the call enters its last quarter.
fact: Gong: star reps raise price in the 38–46 minute window of a one-hour call after building value; win rate is unchanged whether buyer or seller raises it.
impact: A price without a value recap is a cost; a price after a recap is a trade.
act: Happy to give you the number, and let me put it in context first so it means something. You said the current way of working costs you roughly what we discussed every month. The plan that covers exactly that is the one I will quote now, plus GST, and then I will stop talking and let you react.
act_hinglish: Number zaroor bataunga, bas pehle context mein rakh deta hoon taaki uska matlab bane. Aapne kaha tha abhi ka tareeka aapko har mahine roughly utna cost karta hai jitna humne discuss kiya. Jo plan exactly wahi cover karta hai uska price main abhi bataunga, plus GST, aur phir main chup ho jaaunga aur aapko react karne dunga.
question_to_ask: Against the number you described for the current way of working, how does that price land for you?
proof_point: Quote only the capsule price, with GST clarity; then stop talking.
do_not: Do not pad the price with a discount in the same breath; do not avoid the question.
psychology: Anchoring on the cost of the problem before the price reframes the comparison.

title: Last five minutes: book the dated next step
trigger_description: The call is wrapping up or the buyer mentions next steps.
fact: Gong (8,382 deals): 5% close rate without a next-steps discussion vs 20% with one.
impact: 'I'll send a proposal' without a review meeting is where most deals quietly die.
act: Before we wrap up, let us agree the next step now while it is fresh, rather than over email next week. I would suggest Thursday at four with your finance person on the invite, so we go through the proposal together and decide. If Thursday does not work, give me another slot and I will send the invite now.
act_hinglish: Wrap up karne se pehle agla step abhi tay kar lete hain jab tak taaza hai, agle hafte email pe nahi. Main Thursday chaar baje suggest karunga, aapke finance wale ko invite pe rakh ke, jahan hum proposal saath mein dekhein aur decide karein. Agar Thursday nahi chalta toh koi aur slot batayiye aur main phone rakhne se pehle invite bhej dunga.
question_to_ask: Who else should be in that conversation so that we do not need a third call to decide?
proof_point: Send the calendar invite before the call ends; confirm on WhatsApp.
do_not: Do not end the call with 'I'll send something over' and no date.
psychology: A date agreed verbally while the value is fresh is kept; one proposed by email is negotiated.

title: Close: recommend, don't pressure
trigger_description: The buyer raises terms, start dates or onboarding unprompted.
fact: Gong: in closing calls, mechanics don't discriminate; won deals contain buyer concerns about SLAs, implementation, support and terms. JOLT: offer your recommendation and narrow the options.
impact: Late-stage value is in surfacing unraised topics (SLA, support, implementation) and recommending a decision.
act: Based on everything you have told me, my honest recommendation is to start with the smaller option on the date you mentioned, rather than the full rollout. Let me also tell you what support looks like in the first month and who you call when something breaks, because that matters more than the contract wording.
act_hinglish: Aapne jo bhi bataya uske hisaab se meri honest recommendation hai ki poore rollout ki bajaye chhote option se aapki batayi date pe start karein. Saath mein yeh bhi bata deta hoon ki pehle mahine mein support kaisa dikhta hai aur kuch toote toh aap kisko call karenge, kyunki contract ki wording se yeh zyada matter karta hai.
question_to_ask: Is there anything about implementation or support that we have not covered and that would worry your team?
proof_point: Name the SLA and onboarding steps from the capsule.
do_not: Do not use 'offer expires' pressure or a closing technique; Rackham found they hurt higher-priced sales.
psychology: Indecisive buyers need a recommendation and a safety net, not a push.

title: Dated next step with owner and attendees
trigger_description: The buyer offers a vague follow-up instead of a date.
fact: Gong: close rate 5% without a next-step discussion vs 20% with one; winners also multithread (67% more contacts in won deals).
impact: A next step needs a date, an owner and the right attendees or it isn't a step.
act: So that we do not lose the momentum we have built today, can we pencil in a specific time rather than leaving it open? I would suggest Tuesday at eleven, with the person who needs to approve this joining us, and I will send a short agenda tonight so nobody is surprised.
act_hinglish: Taaki aaj jo momentum bana hai woh na khoye, kya hum ek specific time pencil kar sakte hain, khula chhodne ki bajaye? Main Tuesday gyarah baje suggest karunga, jisme approve karne wale insaan bhi join karein, aur main aaj raat ek chhota agenda bhej dunga taaki kisi ko surprise na ho.
question_to_ask: Who needs to be in that meeting for a decision to actually be possible on the day?
proof_point: Calendar invite sent before hanging up; WhatsApp confirmation after.
do_not: Do not accept 'we'll get back to you' as the plan.
psychology: Specific proposals are accepted or corrected; vague ones are deferred.

title: Mutual action plan
trigger_description: The buyer wants to know how this would get done.
fact: A mutual action plan is a shared timeline of buyer and seller tasks working back from go-live or FY-end; practitioner consensus, no close-rate data.
impact: A plan the buyer co-owns survives their internal meetings; a vendor timeline does not.
act: Let us work backwards from the date you need this live and list what each side does by when, including your approvals and our setup. I will send it to you as a one-page plan you can share internally, and we will treat it as our plan, not my timeline imposed on you.
act_hinglish: Jis date tak aapko yeh live chahiye, wahan se peeche chalte hain aur list karte hain ki har side kab tak kya karegi, aapke approvals aur hamara setup dono. Main isko ek page ka plan bana ke bhej dunga jo aap internally share kar sakein, aur yeh hamara plan hoga, meri timeline aap pe thopi hui nahi.
question_to_ask: Which of these steps is most likely to slip on your side, and how do we protect that one?
proof_point: A dated plan with owners on both sides, attached to the follow-up.
do_not: Do not send a generic implementation timeline.
psychology: Shared ownership of the plan converts a buyer into a partner.

title: Anti-patterns: pressure, FOMO, instant discount
trigger_description: You are about to use pressure or a discount to force a decision.
fact: JOLT: when buyers wavered, 73% of reps fell back on the status-quo/FOMO argument; escalating with fear or discounts increased loss likelihood in 84% of those interactions. Rackham: closing techniques hurt higher-priced sales.
impact: Pressure confirms the buyer's fear of messing up; it is the most reliable way to lose an indecisive buyer.
act: Do not use the pressure line. Say instead: I am not going to push you with a deadline, because this should be a decision you are comfortable with. My recommendation is the option we discussed, here is how we would make it safe to start, and I suggest we decide by the end of next week either way.
act_hinglish: Pressure wali line mat boliye. Iski jagah kahiye: Main aapko deadline se push nahi karunga, kyunki yeh aisa decision hona chahiye jisme aap comfortable hon. Meri recommendation wahi option hai jo humne discuss kiya, yeh raha hum isko shuru karna safe kaise banayenge, aur main suggest karunga agle hafte ke end tak decide kar lein, jo bhi decision ho.
question_to_ask: What would need to be true for this to feel like a safe decision rather than a risky one?
proof_point: Risk reversal terms you can honour, not deadlines you invent.
do_not: Do not say 'today only', escalate FOMO, or drop the price in response to hesitation.
psychology: Indecision is driven by fear of messing up; safety, not urgency, resolves it.

title: Buyer indecision: JOLT
trigger_description: The buyer keeps asking for more material or cannot choose between options.
fact: JOLT (2.5M calls): 87% of deals show moderate or high indecision; high indecision wins 6%; JOLT-skilled reps reach up to 31%. Steps: Judge, Offer a recommendation, Limit exploration, Take risk off the table.
impact: More information past the point of usefulness increases indecision. Narrowing options and recommending one reduces it.
act: I think you have seen enough to decide, and honestly one more demo is unlikely to change the picture. If I were in your seat I would pick the option we discussed and start with the smaller scope. Rather than more information, let me make it safe to start, with a pilot you can walk away from.
act_hinglish: Mujhe lagta hai aapne decide karne ke liye kaafi dekh liya hai, aur sach kahun toh ek aur demo se picture badalne wali nahi. Agar main aapki jagah hota toh discuss kiya hua option chunta aur chhote scope se start karta. Aur information ki bajaye, main isko shuru karna safe banaata hoon, ek aise pilot ke saath jisse aap deliver na hone pe nikal sakein.
question_to_ask: Is the hesitation about which option to choose, or about whether to act at all right now?
proof_point: A single recommended option plus a defined pilot or exit.
do_not: Do not send a third reference or schedule a fourth demo.
psychology: Choice, information and expectations overload are the three faces of indecision; reduce all three.
